newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel sets 1998 budget at 461 bln DM - sources.
newsitem.headline: Waigel sets 1998 budget at 461 bln DM - sources.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel has set 1998 budget spending at 461 billion marks ($263 billion), well above an original target of 447 billion marks due to high unemployment costs, coalition sources said on Tuesday.

Waigel, who is due to present his completed 1998 budget proposal together with a 1997 supplementary budget to the cabinet on Friday, has been meeting cabinet ministers this week to fine-tune the budgets for each ministry.

Waigel, struggling to keep Germany's finances under control to qualify for European economic and monetary union (EMU), has been forced to expand the budget because of high unemployment costs and lower-than-expected tax receipts.

The sources from Chancellor Helmut Kohl's centre-right coalition confirmed a report in the Berliner Zeitung daily, released ahead of publication on Wednesday, that about 40 billion marks had been set aside for unemployment costs and the Federal Labour Office.
The sources said the only issue still to be settled in the budget were details surrounding the financing of subsidies for development of the former communist east.
Leading members of Kohl's coalition were due to meet to discuss Waigel's budget proposals on Wednesday evening.
Earlier, coalition sources said Bonn had agreed to spend more than two billion marks in 1998 and 1999 to finance the four-nation Eurofighter jet, to replace ageing Phantom jets from the year 2002.

The sources said Bonn would spend 850 million marks on the project in 1998 and 1.2 billion marks in 1999, assuring that Germany upholds its end of the project and orders 180 Eurofighter planes as planned, news project partners Britain, Italy and Spain had been anxiously awaiting.

The Bonn sources said the agreement on the level of defence spending for 1998 and 1999 reached in budget talks between Waigel and Defence Minister Volker Ruehe assured the project's funding for four years.

According to the agreement on defence spending, Ruehe will have a budget of some 46.8 billion marks ($26.7 billion) next year, nearly unchanged from the 1997 defence budget of 46.3 billion. ($ = 1.752 German Marks)
